          Brighton 5-0 Crystal Palace Stats: Seagulls' Stunning Start to Season Goes on With Astonishing Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 18, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Brighton enjoyed a memorable Premier League victory over their bitter rivals on Sunday. Look back on a huge win with our Brighton vs Crystal Palace stats page.
Diego Gómez scored one of the all-time great Premier League goals as Brighton surged to a 5-0 victory over rivals Crystal Palace on Sunday.
Brighton were 3-0 up inside 10 minutes at the Amex Stadium, where Gómez grabbed the Seagulls’ second goal in stunning fashion.

Jaydee Canvot turned into his own net in the fourth minute, before Gómez caught Walter Benítez off his line when striking from just inside Palace’s half, sending an audacious attempt in over the stranded goalkeeper.
Yasin Ayari added a third for Fabian Hürzeler’s men, with his deflected strike leaving Palace shellshocked on the south coast.
Palace’s already slender hopes of a comeback were completely extinguished four minutes after the break, with Charalampos Kostoulas turning home from Ayari’s deflected pass.
Honest Ahanor crucially blocked Gómez’s stinging volley before Ferdi Kadioglu saw a fierce first-time strike tipped over the bar as Brighton pressed for more.
Jean-Phillipe Mateta should have got Palace onto the scoresheet when he was left unchallenged to get a shot off, but the France international’s effort struck the crossbar.
Jefferson Lerma then saw a header clip the post after he met Adam Wharton’s centre, and Palace’s misery was compounded in the 84th minute.
Luka Vuskovic met a deep cross and header it back over for Jack Hinshelwood, who was on hand to nudge beyond Benitez and cap a sparkling Brighton display.
Since the start of the 2006-07 season, Gómez’s goal ranks as the eighth longest-range in the Premier League at 51.3 metres.
It is the furthest out from which a goal has been scored in the competition since Wayne Rooney (57.7m) for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

But Gómez has been trying his luck from distance plenty during his time at Brighton. The Paraguayan has already tallied four attempts from over 50m out in the Premier League, though this is was the first to result in a goal.
Brighton became the ninth side in Premier League history to score three goals in the first 10 minutes of a match, and first since Newcastle United against Tottenham in April 2023.

They have already scored 23 Premier League goals this season – their most ever at this stage of a campaign in the top four tiers. Indeed, only Barcelona have scored more goals than the Seagulls across Europe’s big-five leagues this term (39). Brighton’s last four league wins have come by an aggregate score of 15-0.
This was Hürzeler’s first victory over Palace, however, with Leicester City the only one of 29 opponents he has failed to beat across all competitions as Brighton boss (P2 D2).

Palace, meanwhile, have already shipped 17 league goals this term, with the Eagles last conceding more at this stage of a season in the top four tiers in 1980-81 (21), and the pressure may well be mounting on Pierre Sage.
